# OPENING — THE DEFENDER

The question is a "who" question, and the record answers a who question with names. It answers it in four voices, from the body of the promised seed, and from the naming act the text gives to Joseph. What it never does is narrate the how — and I will not narrate it either. I affirm the who; I state no mechanism.

---

## 1. THE FATHER IS NAMED — FOUR VOICES [L1]

The mother speaks: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48) [L1] — she says this to the child at twelve years old, and the whole gospel has stood beside "Joseph and his mother marvelled" (Luke 2:33) [L1] and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41) [L1].

The town speaks: "Is not this Joseph's son?" (Luke 4:22) [L1]; "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42) [L1].

A disciple speaks: "We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45) [L1].

The angel speaks: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20) [L1] — and Joseph is "of the house of David" (Luke 1:27, *ek oikou David*, out of the house of David) [L2], "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4) [L1]. Not one of these four voices is ever corrected [L3]. And the naming of the child is Joseph's act: "and he called his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:25) [L1] — the father's act throughout, as with Zacharias, "how he would have him called" (Luke 1:62-63) [L3].

## 2. THE PROMISED SEED IS A FLESH SEED OUT OF A FATHER'S BODY [L1-L2-L3]

"I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) [L1]. "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne" (Psalm 132:11) [L1]. "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3) [L1] — *kata sarka*, according to the flesh, the marker of bodily descent [L2]. "Of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne" (Acts 2:30) [L3] — the same loins-word of the priesthood reckoning (Hebrews 7:5, 10, *osphys*, the loins) [L2]. "It is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14) [L1]. Seed that proceeds out of bowels and loins, evident and sprung out, is not produced by a legal act; a man's body is in the sentence [L4: resting on 2 Samuel 7:12 and Romans 1:3, both stating out-of-the-body flesh descent, with Acts 2:30 as the cross-reference].

## 3. "SON OF GOD" NAMES A COVENANT, NOT A BEGETTER [L1-L3]

God says of Solomon, with David alive and named as his father: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house... for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father" (1 Chronicles 28:6) [L1]; "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14) [L1]. The same title is applied to Jesus at the resurrection: "God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written... Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee" (Acts 13:33) [L3]; "declared to be the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead" (Romans 1:4) [L1]. Luke 1:32 gives the throne "of his father David" and the title together, before the question in verse 34 [L1]; verse 35 says he "shall be CALLED the Son of God" [L1]. A title Solomon bore with a living earthly father, and a title declared at the resurrection, names no begetter of flesh [L4: resting on 1 Chronicles 28:6 [L1] and Acts 13:33 [L3]].

## 4. THE ANGEL'S VERBS ARE PRESENCE AND POWER [L1-L2-L3]

"The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee" (Luke 1:35) [L1]. "Come upon" (*eperchomai*, to come upon) is the same verb as "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you" (Acts 1:8) [L2-L3] — the apostles at Pentecost, of whom the text says "ye shall be witnesses," not that they were begotten. "Overshadow" (*episkiazō*, to overshadow) is the same word as the transfiguration cloud: "a cloud, and overshadowed them" (Luke 9:34) [L2-L3], and of Peter's healing shadow (Acts 5:15) [L3]. Neither verb denotes begetting at any row where the text uses them [L4: resting on the Luke 1:35 [L1] verb pair and the Acts 1:8 / Luke 9:34 [L3] parallels].

## 5. THE QUIET ROWS STATE A STATE AND A MORTALITY, NOT "NO MAN" [L1-L2-L3]

"Of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ" (Matthew 1:16) [L1] — one passive verb (*egennēthē*, was born) after thirty-nine active "begat" rows in the same list [L2]: non-narration, not a denial. "Before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:18) [L1] and "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25) [L1] — held as written: a state at the time, with the naming act given to Joseph in the same verse. "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" (Luke 1:34) [L1] — present tense of a betrothed woman ("espoused to a man whose name was Joseph," Luke 1:27) [L1-L2], and the same Mary calls Joseph "thy father" twelve years later [L3]. "Made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) [L1] is the mortality idiom: "Man that is born of a woman is of few days" (Job 14:1) [L1]; "he which is born of a woman" (Job 15:14) [L1]; "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist" (Matthew 11:11) [L1] — and John's father was named and struck dumb for disbelief (Luke 1:13) [L3]. None of these rows says "no man"; the record simply does not write the how, and neither will I [L4: resting on Matthew 1:18, 1:25 [L1] as stating rows and the Job / Matthew 11:11 [L3] mortality parallel].

The one row the other side will press, "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20) [L1], is origin-language: "of" (*ek*, out of) with God or the Spirit is covenant origin throughout — "born of God" (John 1:13) [L1] — and the biological marker is absent there and present at Romans 1:3 ("according to the flesh") [L1-L2]. The text requires the flesh seed and names the man; it never says no man was involved [L4: resting on John 1:13 [L1] and Romans 1:3's *kata sarka* [L2]].

## 6. THE RECKONING IS BY THE FATHER'S HOUSE [L1-L3]

"By the house of their fathers... every man by their polls" and "declared their pedigrees... by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2, 18) [L1]. Where the register ran by a wife's house, it was struck: those who "could not shew their father's house" were excluded (Ezra 2:59) [L1]; priests named after the wife's house were "as polluted, put from the priesthood" (Ezra 2:61-62) [L1]. Joseph is enrolled accordingly: "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4) [L1]. [L4: resting on Numbers 1:2 [L1] and the Ezra 2:59, 61-62 [L3] inverse rows.]

---

**FLOOR STATEMENT.** The father is named in four voices and never corrected; the promised seed is flesh out of bowels and loins; "Son of God" is a covenant and resurrection title; the angel's verbs are presence and power; the quiet rows state states and mortality and never say "no man"; the reckoning runs by the father's house. So the text both requires a father's body and names the man — while refusing to narrate the how. I hold both fences: I will not say Mary bore a child without a man, and I will not construct a mechanism the text does not write.

D1. Joseph is named as the father by the mother, the narrator and the town: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48) [L1], "Joseph and his mother" (Luke 2:33) [L1], "Is not this Joseph's son?" # OPENING: Did Christ have a biological father?

**Position:** No. The child Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost with no human father. Joseph was his father only by legal reckoning and common opinion.

## 1. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost," not of a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek *gennēthen* means "begotten/conceived," and it is followed by *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of spirit holy." The preposition *ek* gives the source of the begetting. The text names the source as the Holy Ghost, where a human father would otherwise stand. The phrase *prin ē synelthein autous* means "before they came together," so the time of conception is fixed before any union of the two.

**[L1]** Luke 1:34–35: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? … The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Andra ou ginōskō* means "a man I do not know," and *ginōskō* is used here of marital knowledge. *Episkiasei* means "will cast a shadow over," which is the language of divine presence and not of human union. The word *dio* means "therefore," and it makes the divine agency the stated ground of the title "Son of God."

**[L3]** Luke 1:35 and Matthew 1:20 are independent accounts. Matthew gives Joseph's side, with the angel speaking to him in a dream, and Luke gives Mary's side, with the angel speaking to her. Both name the same agent.

## 2. Mary was a virgin, and Joseph did not know her before the birth

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "to a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

**[L2]** *Parthenos* means "virgin." *Egignōsken* is the imperfect of *ginōskō* ("was knowing"), and with *heōs hou* ("until") it limits the point to the birth. I claim only that no union occurred before the birth, and that is all this chain needs.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:22–23 cites Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." **[L2]** The Hebrew is *ʿalmāh*, "a young woman of marriageable age, unmarried." Genesis 24:43 uses the same word of Rebekah, and Genesis 24:16 says of her: "a virgin, neither had any man known her." So the word can carry that sense in the text, and Matthew's *parthenos* fixes it here.

**[L4]** Joseph's reaction rests on Matthew 1:19 ("minded to put her away privily") and Matthew 1:20 ("fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife"). He did not suppose the child was his, and the angel does not correct him by saying it was. Instead the angel assigns the conception to the Holy Ghost. The inference follows from these two verses together with the *ek pneumatos* source in §1.

## 3. Joseph's fatherhood is only supposed

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *Enomizeto* means "was thought, reckoned by custom." Luke himself marks the claim as a belief and not as a fact.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."

**[L2]** Through Matthew 1:2–15 the verb is *egennēsen*, "begat," in an unbroken line of male fathers. At verse 16 the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē*, "was born," and the relative pronoun is *hēs*, feminine singular, "of whom." Joseph is called *ton andra Marias*, "the husband of Mary," and is not said to have begotten. The pattern of "begat" is broken at exactly this point.

**[L3]** John 6:42 ("whose father and mother we know") and Luke 2:48 ("thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing") are the reports of speakers. The first is the crowd and the second is Mary. In Luke 2:49 the child answers, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" That reply corrects the term "father" and transfers it. Luke 3:23 supplies the narrator's own gloss on the matter.

## 4. The human nature came from the woman alone

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *Genomenon ek gynaikos* means "coming to be out of a woman." The text names only the woman as the source of his human origin.

**[L3]** Genesis 3:15 says "her seed." **[L2]** The Hebrew is *zeraʿ*, "seed," and here it is attached to the woman. That is unusual, because seed is ordinarily reckoned through the man. Hebrews 10:5 says "a body hast thou prepared me," with *katērtisō* meaning "you fitted/furnished."

**[L4]** Romans 1:3 says "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." This does not give the child a human father. Luke 1:32 is spoken to Mary: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The Davidic descent is therefore assigned in the angel's word to Mary's child, and the "seed" of Romans 1:3 comes through the woman of Galatians 4:4. Both verses are footings for the inference.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. The conception was out of the Holy Ghost and not out of a man. Footing: Matthew 1:18, 20 [L1], with *gennēthen ek pneumatos hagiou* ("begotten out of spirit holy") [L2], and Luke 1:34–35 [L1], with *andra ou ginōskō* ("a man I do not know") and *episkiasei* ("will cast a shadow over") [L2].
2. Mary was a virgin at conception and Joseph did not know her before the birth. Footing: Luke 1:27 and Matthew 1:25 [L1], with *parthenos* ("virgin") and *egignōsken heōs hou* ("was knowing until") [L2], and Isaiah 7:14 with Genesis 24:16, 43 [L3] on *ʿalmāh* ("young woman, unmarried").
3. Joseph's fatherhood is only supposed and legal. Footing: Luke 3:23 [L1], with *enomizeto* ("was reckoned by custom") [L2], and Matthew 1:16 [L1], with feminine *hēs* ("of whom") breaking the *egennēsen* ("begat") pattern [L2], with Luke 2:48–49 [L3] showing the child transferring the title "father."
4. The human nature of the child came from the woman alone. Footing: Galatians 4:4 [L1], with *ek gynaikos* ("out of a woman") [L2], and Genesis 3:15 [L1], with *zeraʿ* ("seed") attached to the woman [L2], with Hebrews 10:5 and Luke 1:32 [L3].
5. Therefore Christ had no biological father. The child was conceived by the Holy Ghost in Mary, a virgin, and Joseph was only his supposed father.

What is stacked is **commanded content**, portion upon portion, distributed across the place (שָׁם *sham*, "there").

The sentence performs what it names — a line placed against its like, again and again. [L4, footing: [L1] Isa 28:10; [L2] tsav from tsavah, qav, ze'ir, sham, reduplication pattern — chain: repeated like-unit form → additive, incremental pedagogy].

**OPENING — THE QUESTION AND THE TEXT'S OWN CATEGORY**

The topic asks whether Christ had a biological father. The text has its own word for "biological": "according to the flesh" (kata sarka = "according to the flesh"), and it makes its lineage claim in that word. I hold that he did — Joseph, Mary's husband, of the house of David. Three registers of the text carry it: the seed promised out of a man's body [L1][L3], the father named in four voices [L1], and the stated means of begetting [L1][L3], with the contrary rows measured at the word level [L1][L2].

**I. THE SEED IS FLESH SEED OUT OF A MAN'S BODY [L1]**

2 Samuel 7:12 — "And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom." The promised seed proceeds out of the body of David's line.

Psalm 132:11 — "The LORD hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." The throne takes the fruit of the body.

Acts 2:30 — "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;" — "loins" is osphys (G3751 = loins), the same word used of Levi's sons coming "out of the loins of Abraham" (Hebrews 7:5, 10).

Romans 1:3 — "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" and 2 Timothy 2:8 — "Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel". [L3] Hebrews 7:14 — "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda". A seed that "proceeds out of the bowels," "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh," and is "evident," is seed out of a man's body [L3].

**II. THE FATHER IS NAMED, IN FOUR REGISTERS [L1]**

Mary's own mouth — Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The narrator — Luke 2:33 "And Joseph and his mother marvelled"; Luke 2:41 "Now his parents went to Jerusalem". The town — John 6:42 "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"; Luke 4:22 "Is not this Joseph's son?"; a disciple — John 1:45 "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph". The angel — Matthew 1:20 "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife". And Joseph names the child: Matthew 1:21 "thou shalt call his name JESUS"; Matthew 1:25 "and he called his name JESUS" — the father's act, as with Zacharias, to whom the sign was given "how he would have him called" (Luke 1:13, 62-63) [L3]. **III. JOSEPH IS OF THE HOUSE OF DAVID, AND THE CHILD IS RECKONED TO THE FATHER'S HOUSE [L1][L2][L3]**

Luke 1:27 — "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" — ex oikou David ("of the house of David") follows the man Joseph [L2]. Luke 2:4 — "because he was of the house and lineage of David"; Luke 1:32 — "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David".

The reckoning is by the father's house: Numbers 1:2 — "after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their polls"; Numbers 1:18 — "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers". The inverse rows show the rule enforced: Ezra 2:59 "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed" (excluded); Ezra 2:61-62 the children of Barzillai, "called after their name" of the wife's house, "as polluted, put from the priesthood"; Ezra 10:3 puts away the wives "and such as are born of them" [L3]. # Opening: Did Christ have a biological father?

**Position.** No. Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no human male begetter. Joseph was husband and legal guardian, and the people only supposed him to be the father. Jesus was nonetheless truly human, "made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4).

**Definition.** "Biological father" here means a human male who supplied the seed of conception. Everything below tests that question.

---

## I. The genealogy breaks its own pattern

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2-16 uses "begat" about forty times in an unbroken line: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob…". Then the pattern breaks at verse 16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, **of whom was born Jesus**, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb "begat" is ἐγέννησεν (egennēsen, "begat/fathered", active, with a male subject). In verse 16 the active form stops. The text reads ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη Ἰησοῦς (ex hēs egennēthē Iēsous, "out of whom was begotten/born Jesus"). The relative pronoun ἧς (hēs, "whom") is **feminine singular**, so the source of birth is Mary alone, not Joseph or "them." Joseph is called ἀνήρ (anēr, "husband/man"), not "father."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:11-12 names Jechonias in the line, and Jeremiah 22:30 says of him: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David." **[L4]** Footing: Matthew 1:16 (no "begat" for Jesus) and Jeremiah 22:30 (no prospering seed of Jechonias on David's throne). Chain: if Joseph begat Jesus, Jesus would be Jechonias's seed under that decree. Matthew's careful break fits Jesus inheriting the right through Joseph's legal line without Joseph's seed.

## II. Matthew 1:18-25: conceived of the Holy Ghost

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, **before they came together**, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Verse 20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Verse 25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

**[L2]** The phrase is ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου (ek pneumatos estin hagiou, "is out of the Spirit, holy"). ἐκ (ek, "out of") marks source or origin. The participle γεννηθέν (gennēthen, "that which has been begotten/conceived") has the Holy Spirit as its source, with no male source named. In verse 25 ἐγίνωσκεν (eginōsken, "was knowing") in the imperfect with οὐκ (ouk, "not") ἕως (heōs, "until") shows no marital relations through the birth.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35 gives the same source: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee." Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph "minded to put her away privily." He was not the father and knew it, until the angel's word in verse 20 corrected him.

## III. Luke 1:34-35: Mary's question and the answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I **know not a man**?" Verse 35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: **therefore also** that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω (andra ou ginōskō, "a man I do not know") uses the verb for sexual knowledge. ## I. L1 — THE KJV TEXT’S OWN VOCABULARY

**1. John 10:16 states the question in sheep/fold/flock terms, not blood terms.**  
[L1] John 10:16 KJV:  
> “And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.”  

[L1] The text says:  
- “other sheep I have” — they already belong to the Shepherd.  
- “not of this fold” — they are outside the present enclosure.  
- “them also I must bring” — the Shepherd brings them.  
- “they shall hear my voice” — they are sheep by Shepherd-recognition.  
- “one fold, and one shepherd” — the end is unity under one Shepherd.

**2. The saying itself does not name Gentiles, foreigners, or blood.**  
[L1] John 10:16 does not say “Gentiles,” “nations,” “foreigners,” “strangers,” or “blood.”  
[L2] The Greek saying contains:  
> ἄλλα πρόβατα ἔχω ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης· κἀκεῖνά με δεῖ ἀγαγεῖν, καὶ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσουσι, καὶ γενήσεται μία ποίμνη, εἷς ποιμήν.  

It contains **πρόβατα** “sheep,” **αὐλή** “fold/enclosure,” **ποίμνη** “flock,” **ποιμήν** “shepherd.” It does **not** contain αἷμα “blood,” ἔθνη “Gentiles/nations,” ξένοι “foreigners,” or ἀλλογενής “of another race/kind.”  

**3. The distinction in John 10:16 is fold-membership, not species or bloodline.**  
[L2] In John 10:16a, “this fold” translates **ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης**, “out of this fold/enclosure.”  
[L2] In John 10:16b, KJV “one fold” translates **μία ποίμνη**, “one flock.” Thus the KJV uses “fold” twice, but the Greek distinguishes:  
- **αὐλή** = sheepfold/enclosure, the present fold.  
- **ποίμνη** = flock, the united flock after gathering.  

[L4-A] Therefore, John 10:16’s problem is not that the “other sheep” are non-sheep or non-covenant by blood; it is that they are sheep outside the present fold.  
**Footing:** [L1] John 10:16; [L2] αὐλή/ποίμνη distinction; [L1] John 10:27.  
**Chain:** The Shepherd says “I have” them [L1]; αὐλή names the enclosure, not the species or bloodline [L2]; “My sheep hear my voice” identifies the other sheep as His sheep because they hear His voice [L1].

**4. John’s parallel explanation says “children of God scattered abroad,” not “foreign blood.”**  
[L1] John 11:52 KJV:  
> “And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.”  

[L2] Greek:  
> καὶ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον, ἀλλ’ ἵνα καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν.  

The gathering is described as **τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα**, “the children of God, the scattered ones,” gathered **εἰς ἕν**, “into one.”

[L4-B] Therefore, the Johannine parallel to John 10:16 frames the gathering as a gathering of scattered children into one, not a census of ethnic outsiders by blood.  
**Footing:** [L1] John 11:52; [L2] τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, διεσκορπισμένα, εἰς ἕν; [L1] John 10:16.  
**Chain:** John 10:16 says other sheep are brought into one flock [L1]; John 11:52 says the scattered are children of God gathered into one [L1]; the Greek vocabulary is children/scattered/gathered/one, not blood/foreigner [L2].

The standard reading stands: the “other sheep” of John 10:16 are ethnic outsiders to the Judean covenant fold—Gentiles—not the scattered Lo-ammi Northern Kingdom.

**I. The saying, re-seated in its own Greek**

[L1] John 10:16: “And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.”

[L2] The Greek under that English is καὶ ἄλλα πρόβατα ἔχω ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης· κἀκεῖνα δεῖ με ἀγαγεῖν, καὶ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσουσιν, καὶ γενήσονται μία ποίμνη, εἷς ποιμήν (TR: γενήσεται μία ποίμνη). Three lexical facts govern the verse and already break a two-house identification.

First, the enclosure and the unity are different nouns. “This fold” is αὐλή (courtyard, pen, enclosure). The unity clause is not a second αὐλή. It is μία ποίμνη, εἷς ποιμήν—“one flock, one shepherd.” [L1] The KJV prints “fold” in both clauses; [L2] the text it translates does not. Jesus does not promise that the other sheep will be penned inside this αὐλή. He promises that those not of this enclosure, once brought, become one flock under one shepherd. A Judah-plus-Ephraim reunion into one national fold is the wrong shape of the clause. The shape is: sheep outside this pen are led by the same shepherd into one flock.

Second, ἄλλα cannot be pressed into “other of the same ethnic kind.” [L2] John’s Gospel has no ἕτερος. ἄλλος is his only word for “other” (John 14:16 ἄλλον παράκλητον; John 20:30 ἄλλα σημεῖα). A classical same-kind/different-kind distinction is not Johannine grammar, and it is inadmissible here.

Third, the identity mark of the other sheep is future hearing, not tribal recovery: τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσουσιν, under divine necessity (δεῖ με ἀγαγεῖν). κἀκεῖνα (“those also”) sets them beside sheep he already calls, not beside a sister kingdom he has not named.

**II. “This fold” is the community he is addressing; “my sheep” are hearers, not a house**

[L1] John 10 is spoken in Jerusalem to Judeans, after the blind man is cast out of the synagogue (John 9:34–10:1). The αὐλή of the figure is the enclosure he has just entered as door and shepherd (John 10:1–9). He calls his own sheep out by name (John 10:3–4). He does not map the pen onto the divided monarchy. Thief, robber, hireling, and porter have no referent in 722 BC.

[L1] John 10:26–27: “But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.” [L2] οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐκ τῶν προβάτων τῶν ἐμῶν—the men of this very setting, ethnic sons of the southern fold, “are not of my sheep.” The ὅτι ties non-sheep status to unbelief. Hearing (ἀκούουσιν / ἀκούσουσιν) is the criterion in both 10:27 and 10:16.

[L4] Therefore “this fold” cannot mean “House of Judah” as an ethnic bloc, and “other sheep” cannot mean “House of Israel” as the complementary ethnic bloc. Footing: [L1] John 10:26, many inside the Judean audience are not his sheep; [L1] John 10:16, the others are defined by the same hearing, not by a tribal name; [L2] ἐκ τῶν προβάτων is a partitive of response, not of kingdom. If Judah-as-fold were his sheep, 10:26 would be false. The chain, not the bare noun “sheep,” decides the referent.

**III. John himself identifies those beyond “that nation”**

[L1] John 11:51–52: Caiaphas prophesied that Jesus should die “for that nation; And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” [L2] οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον… τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν. “Not for the nation only” is an explicit excess over the ἔθνος Caiaphas meant—the Jewish nation. The ones gathered are named τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, not Ephraim, Joseph, or the ten tribes.

[L1] John 1:12–13 defines that title: “as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God… which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.” [L2] τέκνα θεοῦ by receiving the Son, expressly not by blood. [L3] John 11:52 must be read by John 1:12, not by a tribal glossary John never uses. John does not name the Northern Kingdom, Lo-ammi, or the house of Joseph anywhere in the Gospel. The scattered “children of God” are those who will receive him, beyond that nation.

[L1] John 4:39–42 already shows outsiders to the Judean fold hearing his word and confessing him “the Saviour of the world.” [L2] ὁ σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου. [L1] John 4:9, 4:22: Jews have no dealings with Samaritans; salvation is of the Jews; yet worship will not be bound to Jerusalem or Gerizim (John 4:21–24). Samaritans are not the pure House of Israel. [L1] 2 Kings 17:24–33: the Samaritans are transplanted nations, mixed, and religiously alien to Judah. They are ethnic and covenantal outsiders to “this fold,” and they hear. They are the narrative preview of 10:16, and they falsify a ten-tribe identification.

[L1] John 12:20–23: “certain Greeks” (Ἕλληνές τινες) ask to see Jesus, and Jesus says the hour is come. [L1] John 12:32: “I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.” [L2] πάντας ἑλκύσω. [L3] John 17:2, “power over all flesh”; John 17:20, “Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word.” The “also” of 17:20 matches κἀκεῖνα of 10:16: further believers through the word, not a hidden northern house. [L1] John 1:29 and John 3:16 set the horizon as the world (κόσμος), not as Ephraim.

**IV. The Lo-ammi text, under apostolic application, names Gentiles**

The Northern-Kingdom reading depends on Hosea’s Lo-ammi. The canon does not leave that oracle unnamed.

[L1] Hosea 1:9–10: “Ye are not my people” (לֹא עַמִּי); then, “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” [L2] לֹא־עַמִּי אַתֶּם … בְּנֵי אֵל־חָי.

[L1] Romans 9:24–26 applies that oracle in so many words: “not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles… I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved… in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.” [L2] οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν. Paul does not apply Lo-ammi to a reconstituted ten-tribe kingdom. He applies it to Gentiles called alongside Jews.

[L3] 1 Peter 2:9–10: “which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God” (οἵ ποτε οὐ λαὸς νῦν δὲ λαὸς θεοῦ), set on those called out of darkness. [L3] Acts 15:14: “God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.” [L1] Acts 15:17: “the residue of men… and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called.” When the apostles had to name the people being added, they named Gentiles, and they cited the prophets for that naming.

[L4] A reading that keeps Lo-ammi as the private title of the Northern Kingdom, and then pastes that title onto John 10:16, contradicts the apostolic application of the same oracle. Footing: [L1] Hosea 1:9–10; [L1] Romans 9:24–26; [L3] Acts 15:14. The chain from those footings to the inference is direct: the “not my people” who become God’s people, in the only inspired commentary on Hosea 1 that the debate may use, are Gentiles.

**V. The commission chain: Israel-mission versus those outside it**

[L1] Matthew 10:5–6: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” [L2] εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε· πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ. The contrast is Gentiles and Samaritans over against the house of Israel, and the geography is the towns of Israel, not Assyria. “House of Israel” in that commission is Israel in the land as against ethnic outsiders, not Ephraim as against Judah. The twelve are not sent to recover a Lo-ammi kingdom.

[L1] Matthew 15:24, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel,” belongs to that same restricted ministry. [L1] John 10:16 then names sheep who are not of this fold, whom he must yet bring. If those other sheep were the house of Israel, they would be the flock he was already sent to, and “not of this fold” would be empty. The “must bring” is a further necessity beyond the Israel-mission.

[L3] That further bringing is what the narrative then performs: [L1] Matthew 28:19, “teach all nations”; [L1] Acts 1:8, “Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth”; [L1] Acts 11:18, “Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.” [L4] The other sheep are the ἐθνῶν excluded in Matthew 10:5 and included after the resurrection. Footing: [L1] Matthew 10:5–6 set beside [L1] John 10:16; [L3] Acts 11:18 and Matthew 28:19 as the bringing. Precept upon precept: first the fold (Israel in the land, not Gentiles), then those not of that fold (the nations).

**VI. Prophetic “others” are strangers, and Ezekiel’s “one shepherd” does not rename John’s sheep**

[L1] Isaiah 56:3–8: the son of the stranger (בֶן־הַנֵּכָר) who joins himself to the LORD is brought to the holy mountain; then, “the Lord GOD which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him.” [L2] עוֹד אֲקַבֵּץ עָלָיו לְנִקְבָּצָיו—an additional gathering beyond Israel’s outcasts, in a passage whose subject is the foreigner. [L1] Isaiah 49:6: “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles” (לְאוֹר גּוֹיִם). The prophetic “others beside the gathered of Israel” are ethnic outsiders. That is the Old Testament pattern John 10:16 fits.

The echo of “one shepherd” is real and is not conceded as an identification. [L3] Ezekiel 34:23 and 37:24 promise one shepherd, David, over the flock. [L2] John’s εἷς ποιμήν shares that title. Re-seated in the chain, the echo identifies the shepherd, not the other sheep as Ephraim. Ezekiel 37 reunites two named houses in one land and on two sticks. John 10 never cites the sticks, never says “house of Joseph,” and defines the outside sheep by οὐκ ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης plus hearing. [L1] John 10:26 has already denied that ethnic presence in the southern fold makes one his sheep. [L4] An unidentified verbal echo cannot override John’s own identifiers and the apostolic naming of the added people as Gentiles. Footing: [L1] John 10:16 and 10:26; [L3] Ezekiel 34:23 supplies the shepherd-title only; [L3] Acts 15:14 names the people actually taken. The two-house reading strips “one shepherd” out of that chain and treats one link as the battlefield. It does not break the chain.

**VII. What the standard reading affirms**

[L1] Other sheep, not of this fold, already his (ἔχω), must be brought, will hear, and with those who hear will be one flock under one shepherd. [L2] Outside the αὐλή, not a second Israelite pen; one ποίμνη. [L3] Beyond that nation, children of God by reception, not by blood; Greeks drawn in; Gentiles called “my people” under Hosea’s own words; a people taken from the Gentiles for his name. The scattered Lo-ammi Northern Kingdom is not the referent John states, not the referent John defines, and not the referent the apostles give to the oracle that reading requires.

DECLARED CHAIN
1. Sheep-status in this discourse is hearing the shepherd, not house-membership: Judeans of the present setting who do not believe “are not of my sheep” ([L1] John 10:26–27), and the other sheep are marked by that same hearing ([L1] John 10:16; [L2] ἀκούσουσιν / οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐκ τῶν προβάτων τῶν ἐμῶν).

ANSWER: The “other sheep” of John 10:16 are ethnic outsiders—Gentiles, not of the Judean covenant fold—not the scattered Lo-ammi Northern Kingdom, because they are οὐκ ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης yet hear and become one flock ([L1] John 10:16; [L2] αὐλή ≠ ποίμνη, identity by ἀκούω), and the added “not my people” are named Gentiles ([L1] Rom 9:24–26; [L3] Acts 15:14).

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

The standard reading of Ezekiel 37 is fixed by the prophet’s own glosses, not by a later identity key. The dry bones are the whole house of Israel. The two sticks are the two named houses of that one house — Judah and Joseph/Ephraim — joined into one nation under one Davidic king. The two-house framework is therefore textually real as the schism and its end. It stops at the oracle’s own “no more,” and at the canon’s count of belonging: seed by promise, not a flesh-census of the nations.

I. The bones are identified, not left as a riddle

[L1] Ezekiel 37:11 gives the vision’s glossary in an equative, not a riddle: “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts.” The lament is the nation’s own: death-in-exile, hope lost, cut off. [L1] Ezekiel 37:12–14 answers that lament with graves opened, the people brought “into the land of Israel,” and the LORD’s breath put in them so that they live — “I the LORD have spoken it, and performed it.”

[L2] The Hebrew is a demonstrative identification, not an open simile: הָעֲצָמוֹת הָאֵלֶּה כָּל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵמָּה — “these bones, the whole house of Israel they are.” hēmmâ closes the equation. kol-bêt yiśrāʾēl is the subject-name. The reviving agent is rûaḥ (37:9, 14), the LORD’s breath, not a genealogical discovery. Nothing in the clause renames the bones as the heathen, as a hidden subset, or as a blood-roll waiting to be taken among the nations.

[L3] The immediately prior oracle uses the same addressee and the same sequence. Ezekiel 36:24–28: “I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land,” cleanse you, give “a new heart,” and “put my spirit within you.” Chapter 37:1–14 is that gathering and that spirit enacted as resurrection of the named house. [L3] The cut-off lament also sits on the covenant threat already spoken to this people (Leviticus 26:33, 38; Deuteronomy 30:1–5): scatter, perish among the heathen, then gather from the nations into the land. The bones vision is that restoration, addressed to the house the threat named.

A reading that makes the bones “Gentiles who are Israel by descent, though the text does not say so” strips the glossary. The glossary is the chain. Isolated “bones,” isolated “cut off,” prove nothing until reseated in 37:11–14 and 36:24–28.

II. The two sticks are inscription-identified, and both inscriptions are Israel

[L1] Ezekiel 37:16 commands two writings, not two blank symbols: one stick, “For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions”; the other, “For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions.” [L1] Ezekiel 37:17, 19: they are joined “one to another into one stick,” and the LORD says, “I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand.”

[L2] The object is עֵץ (ʿēṣ) — wood, stick, staff. Identity is not in the timber; it is in the inscription. The first writing is לִיהוּדָה וְלִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲבֵרָיו — for Judah and for the children of Israel his companions (ḥăḇērāw, his associates). The second is לְיוֹסֵף עֵץ אֶפְרַיִם וְכָל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲבֵרָיו — for Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all the house of Israel his companions. Verse 19 varies the second party as שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (šibṭê yiśrāʾēl), “the tribes of Israel his fellows.” Both sticks carry Israel-vocabulary: bənê yiśrāʾēl, kol-bêt yiśrāʾēl, šibṭê yiśrāʾēl. Neither inscription reads “the heathen,” “the nations,” or “the Gentiles.” Unity is לַאֲחָדִים בְּיָדֶךָ / אֶחָד בְּיָדִי — made one in the hand — a divine act of joining named parties, not a census that finds they were already one flesh under other names.

[L3] Those names already have a schism-history. 1 Kings 12:19–20: “Israel rebelled against the house of David,” and “there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.” The prophetic name of the northern house is Ephraim. Isaiah 7:17 marks “the day that Ephraim departed from Judah.” Hosea 5:3 speaks “O Ephraim… O Israel” as one northern address. Jeremiah 3:18 promises the repair in the same two names Ezekiel writes: “the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel,” coming “to the land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers.” Ezekiel’s two sticks are that schism and that repair, under the labels the earlier texts already used.

Therefore “two-house” is warranted inside this chain: house of Judah and house of Joseph/Ephraim, companions and tribes of Israel on both writings, one stick in the LORD’s hand. It is not warranted as a cipher in which one stick secretly means “the Gentile nations discovered to be Ephraim by blood.” That cipher must erase the inscriptions. The inscriptions are the ammunition, and they say Israel on both sticks.

III. The oracle itself ends the two-house state

[L1] Ezekiel 37:21–22 states the reunion’s shape and its negation: “I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” [L1] Ezekiel 37:23–26 continues the “no more”: they shall not defile themselves any more; “so shall they be my people, and I will be their God”; “David my servant shall be king over them”; “they shall dwell in the land… wherein your fathers have dwelt… and my servant David shall be their prince for ever”; “I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant.” [L1] Ezekiel 37:28 keeps a witness-distinction at the climax: “the heathen shall know that I the LORD do sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them for evermore.”

[L2] The stop is lexical, not inferred from silence. גּוֹי אֶחָד (gôy ʾeḥād), מֶלֶךְ אֶחָד (melek ʾeḥād), then וְלֹא יִהְיוּ־עוֹד לִשְׁנֵי גוֹיִם וְלֹא יֵחָצוּ עוֹד לִשְׁתֵּי מַמְלָכוֹת — “they shall not be any more two nations, and they shall not be divided any more into two kingdoms.” The particle עוֹד (ʿôd) with the negative is a terminus: the dual condition ceases. יֵחָצוּ is “be divided” (from חָצָה). What ends is šənê gôyim and šətê mamlāḵôt — the two-nation, two-kingdom state the sticks named. The covenant is בְּרִית עוֹלָם (bərît ʿôlām), an everlasting covenant, with David עַבְדִּי as king and נָשִׂיא forever. Verse 28’s הַגּוֹיִם (haggôyim) are the knowers (וְיָדְעוּ); יִשְׂרָאֵל is the sanctified (מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל). At the oracle’s end the nations are not reclassified as Israel. They know what the LORD does to Israel.

[L3] The same terminus is already in the prophets Ezekiel is not inventing. Hosea 1:11: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head.” Isaiah 11:12–13: the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah are gathered, and “Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim” — the envy ends; the names are not reassigned to other peoples. Jeremiah 31:31: “a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah” — both houses, one covenant. The king is the Davidic promise reseated: 2 Samuel 7:12–16, seed and throne established; Jeremiah 30:9, “they shall serve the LORD their God, and David their king”; Ezekiel 34:23–24, the same “David my servant” as one shepherd over one flock, immediately before this chapter. [L3] Luke 1:32–33 seats that throne-promise on the son of David whose kingdom has no end — the canon’s identification of the one king, not a cancellation of Ezekiel’s land, covenant, or house-names.

The two-house framework’s stop-line is therefore inside Ezekiel 37, not imported against it. The framework describes a division the text says will not continue: no more two nations, no more two kingdoms, one king, one people, one everlasting covenant. A use of “two-house” that keeps the dual as a standing identity key — sorting the world indefinitely into Judah-by-flesh and Ephraim-by-flesh — contradicts the ʿôd-negation it claims to honor. The division is what the joining ends.

IV. “From among the heathen” is locus, not a new name for Ephraim

[L1] Ezekiel 37:21’s preposition does the distinguishing: “I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone.” The children of Israel are the object taken. The heathen are the among-which, the place they have gone. [L1] Ezekiel 37:28, already noted, leaves the heathen as those who know that Israel is sanctified. The dispersion formula never says the heathen are the stick of Ephraim.

[L2] מִבֵּין הַגּוֹיִם (mibên haggôyim) is “from among the nations.” bənê yiśrāʾēl and haggôyim are not interchangeable slots in this sentence. To collapse them is to delete min-bên. The same distinction holds in 36:24, the prior link of the chain.

This is where the extension leaves the text. The claim “the stick of Ephraim is the Gentile nations, because Israel was scattered among them” treats the place of exile as an identity verdict. The verse that mentions the heathen uses them as location and, in v. 28, as witnesses. That is the chain. A term stripped off — “heathen,” “scattered,” “Ephraim” — and reassembled into a blood-census is not the oracle.

V. The canon’s belonging-word is seed by promise; flesh is refused as the count

The topic’s question is not only what the two houses are in Ezekiel, but where that framework stops when later texts speak of who belongs. The stop is the counting rule, and it is stated, not inferred from a modern map.

[L1] Romans 9:6–8: “they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.” [L2] οὐ πάντες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ, οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ — not all who are from Israel are Israel. οὐδʼ ὅτι εἰσὶν σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ, πάντες τέκνα — being Abraham’s sperma does not by itself make all children. τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκός, ταῦτα οὐ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ — the children of the flesh are not, as such, the children of God. τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας λογίζεται εἰς σπέρμα — the children of the promise are counted (logizetai) for the seed. The verb is reckoning, not a blood-roll. A flesh-referent offered as the identity verdict is the move this sentence denies.

# Opening: Jesus had no biological human father

**Position.** The KJV teaches that Jesus had a biological mother, Mary, and no biological human father. His conception was of the Holy Ghost. Joseph stood in the place of a father legally and in the household, and was not the begetter. [L4, resting on the chain below]

By "biological father" I mean the man who supplies the seed of begetting (Greek *gennaō*, to beget; Hebrew *yālad*, to bear or beget).

---

## I. Matthew 1: the genealogy breaks its own pattern

**1.** [L1] Matthew 1:2-15 runs "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob..." down to "Jacob begat Joseph." Verse 16 then reads: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, **of whom was born Jesus**, who is called Christ."

**2.** [L2] The verb "begat" throughout is *egennēsen* (he begat), active voice, with a man as subject. In verse 16 the verb changes to *egennēthē* (was born), passive voice. The relative pronoun is *hēs* (of whom), **feminine singular**, so the birth is "out of her" alone. Had Joseph been the begetter, the established formula "Joseph begat Jesus" was ready to hand. Matthew abandons it at the one place it would matter.

**3.** [L2] Joseph is called *andra* (husband, or man) of Mary. The word names his marital standing and not his fatherhood.

## II. Matthew 1:18-25: the source of the conception is stated

**4.** [L1] "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, **before they came together**, she was found with child **of the Holy Ghost**" (Matthew 1:18).

**5.** [L2] *Prin ē sunelthein autous* means "before they came together". It places the pregnancy before any union. *Ek pneumatos hagiou* means "out of spirit holy": the source (*ek*, out of) of the conception is the Holy Ghost.

**6.** [L1] The angel tells Joseph: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). Joseph had been "minded to put her away privily" (1:19). That reaction makes no sense if he were the father. [L4, resting on 1:19 and 1:20]

**7.** [L2] "That which is conceived" is *to gennēthen* (that which has been begotten or conceived), **neuter**, and the same *ek* (out of) is used. The angel assigns the begetting to the Holy Ghost and not to Joseph.

**8.** [L1] "[Joseph] knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25). [L2] *Ouk eginōsken* (was not knowing) is imperfect tense, a continued state. *Heōs hou* (until which) marks the time up to the birth, and it covers the whole conception and pregnancy.

## III. Luke 1: Mary's own testimony

**9.** [L1] Luke 1:27 calls Mary "a virgin" (*parthenon*, virgin). In 1:34 she asks: "How shall this be, **seeing I know not a man**?"

**10.** [L2] *Epei andra ou ginōskō* uses a present-tense verb, "I am not knowing a man". It is not a future vow. She states her present condition, and the angel's answer takes it as true.

**11.** [L1] The angel answers: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God" (Luke 1:35).

**12.** [L2] *Episkiasei* (will overshadow) is the verb used for the cloud over the tabernacle in the LXX of Exodus 40:35. It signals divine action, not human union. *Dio kai* (therefore also) makes the divine act the stated ground for the title Son of God. [L3, Exodus 40:35 and Luke 1:35]

## IV. Isaiah 7:14 and "a woman"

**13.** [L1] Matthew 1:22-23 says the conception took place "that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."

**14.** [L2] The Hebrew in Isaiah 7:14 is *ʿalmāh* (young woman of marriageable age). I grant that the Hebrew word does not by itself say "never touched". Matthew, however, quotes the Greek *parthenos* (virgin). The Spirit-given use of *ʿalmāh* for Rebekah in Genesis 24:43 sits beside *bĕtûlāh* (virgin) and "neither had any man known her" in 24:16. [L3, Genesis 24:16, 24:43]

**15.** [L1] "God sent forth his Son, **made of a woman**, made under the law" (Galatians 4:4). [L2] *Genomenon ek gunaikos* (coming to be out of a woman) names only the woman as source. [L3] This agrees with Genesis 3:15, "her seed" (Hebrew *zeraʿ*, seed), where the seed is credited to the woman.

## V. Biological descent runs through the mother

**16.** [L1] "[Jesus Christ] was made of the seed of David **according to the flesh**" (Romans 1:3). Acts 2:30 says "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ."

**17.** [L2] *Kata sarka* (according to flesh) is bodily descent. [L3] Luke 3:31 traces a line through Nathan, son of David. Jesus therefore had real human flesh and real Davidic descent, and this is carried by Mary. [L4, resting on Romans 1:3, Luke 3:31 and Matthew 1:16]

**18.** [L1] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." [L2] *Katērtisō* (thou hast fitted or prepared) points to a provided body and not an inherited one.

## VI. Objections answered

**Objection: Luke 2:33, 2:48 and John 6:42 call Joseph his father.**
[L1] Luke 3:23 settles the usage: "being (as was **supposed**) the son of Joseph." [L2] *Hōs enomizeto* (as was thought or reckoned) marks it as opinion. In Luke 2:48 Mary says "thy father and I have sought thee," and the next verse has Jesus correct the title: "wist ye not that I must be about **my Father's** business?" (Luke 2:49). [L3] John 6:42 reports what the crowd says ("whose father and mother we know"), and Luke 3:23 corrects that report. In Luke 2:33, the narrator's "Joseph and his mother" is household language, the same as "his parents" (2:41), and 1:34-35 and 3:23 govern it. [L4, resting on Luke 3:23 and 2:49]

**Objection: Joseph's descent from David is needed for the throne.**
[L1] Matthew 1:20 calls Joseph "son of David," and Matthew 1:16 passes through Jechonias (1:11-12). [L1] Jeremiah 22:30 says of Coniah, "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David." [L4] A begotten son of Joseph would be Coniah's seed, which would put the throne claim under that word. The virgin conception, with descent from David through Mary (Luke 3:31), avoids the difficulty. This is secondary support and not a load-bearing link. [L4, resting on Matthew 1:11-12, Jeremiah 22:30 and Luke 3:31]

---

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Matthew 1:16 drops the active "begat" (*egennēsen*, he begat) of verses 2-15 for the passive "was born" (*egennēthē*, was born) with the feminine "of whom" (*hēs*, of whom). The genealogy therefore withholds the begetting from Joseph. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:2-16, [L2] *egennēsen/egennēthē* and feminine *hēs*, [L3] contrast with the unbroken pattern of verses 2-15.
2. The source of the conception is stated as the Holy Ghost, before Joseph and Mary came together. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18-20 and 1:25, [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of spirit holy), *prin ē sunelthein* (before coming together), neuter *to gennēthen* (that which is begotten), [L3] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 agree on the same source.
3. Mary was a virgin at conception, and the angel names divine overshadowing as the cause. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:27, 1:34-35, [L2] *parthenos* (virgin), present-tense *ou ginōskō* (I am not knowing), *episkiasei* (will overshadow), [L3] Isaiah 7:14 as quoted in Matthew 1:23, and Exodus 40:35.
4. Calling Joseph "father" is household or legal usage and supposition, and the text corrects it. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23 and 2:48-49, [L2] *hōs enomizeto* (as was supposed), [L3] John 6:42 (the crowd's report) answered by Luke 3:23.
5. Jesus had real human descent through the woman alone: "made of a woman" and "of the seed of David according to the flesh." Footing: [L1] Galatians 4:4, Romans 1:3, [L2] *ek gunaikos* (out of a woman), *kata sarka* (according to flesh), [L3] Genesis 3:15, Luke 3:31, Acts 2:30.
6. Jesus had no biological human father. His conception was of the Holy Ghost, Mary was his only biological parent, and Joseph was not the begetter. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16-25, Luke 1:34-35, Luke 3:23, [L2] *egennēthē*/*hēs*, *ek pneumatos hagiou*, *ou ginōskō*, *hōs enomizeto*, [L3] Galatians 4:4, Romans 1:3, Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23, carried through links 1-5.

The standard reading of [L1] John 10:16 stands as the only textually coherent position: the "other sheep" are ethnic outsiders (Gentiles) whom Christ unites with believing Jews to form a single, undivided body (the Church). The challenger’s assertion that the "other sheep" are merely the scattered Northern Kingdom (the House of Israel) violently truncates the explicit scope of the Messianic mandate and ignores the precise lexical boundaries established in the text. 

Here is the affirmative defense of the standard reading.

**I. The Boundary of "This Fold"**
Christ begins by establishing a baseline: "And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold" ([L1] John 10:16). We must first identify "this fold." 
[L2] The Greek noun used here for "fold" is αὐλή (*aulē*), which denotes a walled courtyard or a physical, bounded enclosure. 
[L3] Jesus Himself geographically and ethnically defined the boundary of His earthly ministry in [L1] Matthew 15:24: "I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel." Furthermore, Paul confirms that Christ was "a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God" ([L3] Romans 15:8). 
[L4] "This fold" therefore refers exclusively to the recognized, physical Jewish covenant community (the circumcised nation) of Christ's earthly ministry. This [L4] inference rests squarely on the bounded nature of the noun ([L2] αὐλή) and the explicit, stated limits of His primary mission ([L3] Matthew 15:24).

**II. The Nature of the "One Fold"**
Christ then promises an integration: "them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd" ([L1] John 10:16). 
[L2] In the original Greek, Christ does not say there will be "one *aulē*" (walled courtyard). He shifts the noun. The text reads μία ποίμνη (*mia poimnē*)—meaning "one flock." 
[L3] This lexical shift is exegetically paramount because it aligns perfectly with the apostolic revelation of the mystery of Christ in [L1] Ephesians 2:14, where Christ "hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us." 
[L4] The union of the sheep does not result in bringing outsiders into the walled courtyard (Judaism) or rebuilding the divided kingdoms of Israel into a physical enclosure, but rather creates an entirely new, wall-less entity (the Church). This [L4] inference rests on the lexical shift from courtyard to flock ([L2] *poimnē*) and the cross-reference of the broken partition wall ([L3] Ephesians 2:14).

**III. The Identity of the "Other Sheep"**
The challenger will attempt to force the "other sheep" into the identity of the scattered Northern Kingdom (Ephraim/Israel). The text explicitly forbids this limitation.
[L1] Isaiah 49:6 defines the scope of the Messiah's gathering: "It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth."
[L3] The Northern Kingdom, no matter how scattered or "Lo-ammi" (not my people), remains intrinsically part of the "tribes of Jacob." Yet Isaiah 49:6 separates the restoration of *all* the tribes of Jacob from the ultimate, greater gathering of the Gentiles.
[L4] The "other sheep" must be ethnic outsiders (Gentiles). If the "other sheep" were merely the scattered House of Israel, Christ would only be fulfilling the "light thing" (raising up the tribes of Jacob) while abandoning the ultimate decree of His salvation reaching the uncircumcised nations. This [L4] inference rests irrefutably on the Old Testament mandate separating Jacob from the Gentiles ([L1] Isaiah 49:6) and the New Testament fulfillment where the "aliens from the commonwealth of Israel" are brought near ([L3] Ephesians 2:11-13).

The text of John 10:16 cannot be constrained to an intra-Israelite reunion. It is the Savior’s declaration of the inclusion of the Gentile world.

***

DECLARED CHAIN
1. [L4] "This fold" of John 10:16 designates the recognized, physically bounded Jewish covenant community, resting on the enclosed-courtyard noun ([L2] αὐλή) and Christ's explicitly restricted earthly mission ([L3] Matthew 15:24).
2. [L4] The promised "one fold" of John 10:16 is a wall-less body distinct from the Jewish courtyard, resting on the lexical shift to 'flock' ([L2] ποίμνη) and the apostolic doctrine of breaking the partition wall ([L3] Ephesians 2:14).
3. [L4] The gathering of sheep outside the original fold enacts the Messianic mandate to reach beyond all of Israel, resting on the explicit prophetic distinction between the "tribes of Jacob" and the "Gentiles" ([L1] Isaiah 49:6).
4. [L4] Therefore, the "other sheep" of John 10:16 are ethnic outsiders (Gentiles), gathered with believing Jews into one flock, resting on the lexical shift in the Greek text ([L2] ποίμνη) and the prophetic mandate to reach beyond all tribes of Israel ([L3] Isaiah 49:6).

# OPENING — DEFENDER

The record stands on its own reading, already held in the live corpus (Conclusion #45, ESTABLISHED L1-L2-L3; Conclusion #39, ESTABLISHED L1-L2; DG-19). I open it and defend it. The question is a question of identity: who the "other sheep" are. The record's answer, held at L3 and never pressed to L1: the scattered, Lo-ammi House of Israel. The ethnic-outsider closure is the standard reading, and it is not stated by the text.

## [L1] — THE TEXT, READ WHOLE (DG-27: verse → passage → chapter)

John 10:16 [L1]: *"And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, [and] one shepherd."*

Three phrases carry the case at the KJV floor:

1. **"other sheep I have"** — the sheep are already His before the bringing. Not recruits, not converts acquired later: possessions held at the moment of speaking. [L1, per Conclusion #45]
2. **"which are not of this fold"** — a second *fold* that exists, distinguished from "this fold." The verse sets fold against fold, not sheep against non-sheep. [L1]
3. **"them also I must bring... and there shall be one fold, [and] one shepherd"** — the mission's shape is GATHERING, a reunification under one shepherd, not the addition of outsiders to an unrelated body. [L1]

The passage context agrees [L1]: the Good Shepherd "giveth his life for the sheep" (John 10:11), the wolf "scattereth the sheep" (10:12), the hireling flees (10:12-13), and the Shepherd "calleth his own sheep by name" (10:3) — "my sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me" (10:27). The sheep of v.16 answer to 10:27's mark: they *hear His voice*. That is the identifying signature, and it is His to apply [L1, DG-12].

## [L2] — THE WORDS

Per Conclusion #45's lexical floor [L2]:

- **"other" = allos (G243)**, "else, i.e. different (in many applications)" — it says *other*, not same-kind (1 Corinthians 15:39 uses allos of flesh of a different kind). But what KIND the others are is carried by the noun beside it —
- **"sheep" = probaton (G4263)** — a sheep, a quadruped of the flock. The other ones are SHEEP already. The kind-word settles the category before any field question is asked.
- **"I have" = echo (G2192)**, "to hold... such as possession" — ownership precedes the bringing.
- **"this fold" = aule (G833)** — "a yard... court, (sheep-)fold, hall, palace": a specific enclosure. **"one fold" = poimne (G4167)** — "a flock... fold," a *different Greek word* that the KJV nonetheless prints "fold." The text distinguishes aule (the enclosure the sheep are not of) from poimne (the one flock they are brought into). One flock, not one building.
- **"must" = dei (G1163)**, "it is necessary (as binding)" — the bringing is obligation, covenant necessity, not opportunistic expansion. [L2; DG-19 FULLER]
- **"one shepherd" = heis (G1520)** — the same numeral John 11:52 uses of "gather together in one" (Conclusion #59). Ezekiel 34:23's "one shepherd" is ro'eh *echad* (H259), a different word in a different language (Conclusion #39) — the prophets and the Gospel converge on the *arrangement* (one shepherd over one gathered flock), never on word-identity.

## [L3] — THE CROSS-REFERENCES (the layer at which this conclusion is HELD)

The record does not argue this from John 10:16 alone. It is a chain, precept upon precept [L3, DG-61]:

- **Matthew 15:24 [L1]**: "I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel." The Shepherd's own stated target field, and Matthew 10:5-6 fences it (Conclusion #67, #69). The mission's sheep are Israel-named at the floor.
- **Ezekiel 34:11-12, 23 [L1]**: "I, even I will seek my sheep... I will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day" (Conclusion #38) — "I will set up one shepherd over them... my servant David" (Conclusion #39, #10). The seeking-sheep and the one-shepherd promise are Ezekiel's, and Ezekiel names his flock: "they, [even] the house of Israel, [are] my people... ye my flock" (34:30-31).
- **Ezekiel 37:17, 19, 22 [L1]**: "they shall become one in thine hand" (echad, 8 times in vv.17-22, Conclusion #9) — "they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all." Two houses made one: this is the aule→poimne shape in prophecy.
- **John 11:52 [L1]**: "he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad" — dieskorpismena (G1287), the same root as John 10:12's scatter-verb (Conclusion #46). The scattered children of God and the scattered sheep share the author and the root. And #59 holds the pericope's own two-body structure: "that nation" (the perishable Judean polity of 11:48-50) and the scattered children are distinguished by the text's not-only/but-also.

On this footing the record reads John 10:16 as the gathering of Ezekiel 34 and 37 under one shepherd: the other sheep are the scattered house of Israel, living Lo-ammi ("not my people," Hosea 1:9-10, Sight 521), already His, brought in to hear His voice. **Held at L3 per DG-19 — never stated as L1.** Conclusion #45 carries this exact rating.

## THE LIMIT, STATED ON ITS FACE

This case issues **no per-person verdict and no blood census** [L1-L3, DG-1, DG-12, DG-20, DG-60]. The text counts seed by promise (Romans 9:8, logizomai — DG-12's counting correction), not flesh. "The other sheep" is answered at the level the text answers it: a flock-identity, an arrangement, a mission-shape. The Shepherd names the sheep (John 10:3, 10:27, 10:14); the study names the markers. Ephesians 2:11-12 names *status, not origin* (Conclusion #2) and cannot be spent as a lineage verdict by either side.

And the opposition's closure carries a verdict the text does not state. To say "the other sheep were simply ethnic Gentiles from outside Jacob" is to assert a flesh-referent — a who-belongs verdict in the ethnic vocabulary — with no L1 warrant anywhere in John 10, in the Johannine pericope, or in the prophets Christ's imagery answers. "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne" (Psalm 132:11). "Of whom was born Jesus... concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne" (Acts 2:30). "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14). "Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead" (2 Timothy 2:8). [L2] "Bowels" is *mimme'eykha* — out of the inward parts; "seed" is *sperma*; and Paul's own marker for biological flesh is *kata sarka* — "according to the flesh" — which he attaches twice (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30); "loins" is *osphys*, the same word Hebrews 7:5, 10 uses for human descent. Seed proceeding out of bowels, fruit of loins, according to the flesh, evident — that is the text's own anatomy of descent. A seed that is "evident," "sprang out of Juda," "of the fruit of his loins," cannot stand with no man.

**2. The father is named — in five voices.** [L1] The mother: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48). The public: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42); "Is not this Joseph's son?" (Luke 4:22). A disciple: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45). The narrator: "Joseph... being of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4); "his parents" (Luke 2:41); "Joseph and his mother marvelled" (Luke 2:33). The angel: "Joseph, thou son of David... thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:20–21), and "he called his name JESUS" (1:25) — the father's naming act. [L2] Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" — *enomizeto*, the same verb form as Acts 16:13 "where prayer was *wont* to be made": it marks usage and custom, not a denial. [L3] The named father carries the promised line: "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4) answers "thy seed after thee" (2 Samuel 7:12).

**3. The Spirit-rows name covenant origin, not biological paternity.** [L1] "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). [L2] "of" is *ek*; the New Testament's *ek* + God/Spirit is covenant origin at every row — "born of God" (John 1:13), "born of God" (1 John 3:9), "is of God" (1 John 4:7). Where flesh descent is meant, the writer marks it: "of the seed of David *according to the flesh*" (Romans 1:3). Matthew 1:20 carries no *kata sarka*, because it is not naming flesh origin. Luke 1:35's verbs are not begetting words: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon [*eperchomai*] thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow [*episkiazō*] thee" — [L3] *eperchomai* is the Pentecost word, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you" (Acts 1:8, of the apostles empowered; Luke 24:49), and *episkiazō* is the presence-cloud word, "a cloud overshadowed them" (Luke 9:34; Matthew 17:5; Mark 9:7) and Peter's healing shadow (Acts 5:15). Anointing and presence, at every row.

**4. "Son of God" cannot answer this question — it is a covenant title borne by men with living fathers.** [L1] "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14) — said of Solomon, whose father was David. "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father" (1 Chronicles 28:6) — in one verse, the son David begat and the title God gave. [L3] "This day have I begotten thee" (Psalm 2:7) is applied by Paul to the resurrection, not the conception: "God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus" (Acts 13:33); "declared to be the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead" (Romans 1:4).

**5. What the three quiet rows say — held exactly as written.** [L1] "of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ" (Matthew 1:16) — *egennēthē*, one passive after thirty-nine active begetting-verbs; it narrates no how and denies nothing. [L2] "seeing I know not a man" (Luke 1:34) is *andra ou ginōskō*, present indicative — her state at the moment of speaking to an espoused woman (Luke 1:27); it is not a vow sentence. [L1] "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18) and "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (1:25) — quoted as written, carried as written. [L1] "made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) is the mortality idiom, [L3] "man that is born of a woman is of few days" (Job 14:1; 15:14; 25:4) — the same phrase the Lord uses of John the Baptist (Matthew 11:11), whose father Zacharias is named (Luke 1:13).

Therefore the record forbids **both** moves: it forbids "no man was involved" — the flesh seed rows will not carry it — and it forbids narrating the conception how, because no row narrates it. The question asked is the WHO question, and the text answers it in five voices.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological human father

**Position.** "Biological father" means a male parent who supplies the seed of the child's conception. The KJV text says the child's conception was *of the Holy Ghost*, within a virgin, with no man involved. Joseph was husband, legal father and guardian, but not begetter.

## 1. The text states the mode of conception

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *sunerchomai* (G4905), "to come together," is the verb for the couple's union. The text places the conception before that union. *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537 + G4151 + G40), "out of the Holy Ghost," gives the source of the pregnancy with the preposition *ek*, "out of," marking origin.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *to gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "that which is begotten or conceived," is the same root used for the human "begats" of Matthew 1. Here the begetting is attributed to the Holy Ghost, not to a man.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the conception before any union with Joseph. Matthew 1:20, through *gennaō* with *ek*, assigns the origin of the conceived child to the Holy Ghost. So no human male is the origin of the child, which excludes a biological human father. This rests on two [L1] verses and two [L2] grounds.

## 2. Mary's own testimony and the angel's answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," is used here of sexual knowledge. *anēr* (G435) is "a man," a male. Mary is betrothed, so the question concerns the manner of conception, not the future.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow," and *eperchomai* (G1904), "to come upon," describe divine action. *dio kai* (G1352), "therefore also," makes the divine action the stated reason for the title.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Mary is called a virgin before the angel speaks.

**[L4]** The angel answers "how" with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, not with a man. Luke 1:27 says she was a virgin and Luke 1:34 says she knew no man. Together these show the angel's answer replaces human paternity. A biological father would not need "therefore" to ground the title.

## 3. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Every earlier link in Matthew 1 uses *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," with a male subject. At the last link the verb becomes passive, *egennēthē*, "was born." The relative pronoun *ex hēs* (G1537), "out of whom," is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone. Joseph is called *anēr* (G435), "husband," not begetter.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

**[L4]** The chain of "begat" ends at Joseph, and the birth is "of whom," feminine, namely Mary. Matthew 1:25 repeats the verb *ginōskō*, "know," for Joseph and Mary, and says he did not know her until the child was born. The verse and the Greek grammar together show Joseph's role changes from begetter to husband.

## 4. Joseph's reaction and the "as was supposed"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

**[L4]** Joseph knew he had not fathered the child, and resolved to put Mary away until the angel spoke. This is Joseph's own judgment on the facts, and it is corrected only by the angel, who says the child is "of the Holy Ghost," not by any claim that Joseph was the father.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*), "was reckoned, was supposed by custom," marks the common opinion as an opinion, not as the truth.

Ezekiel 34 and 37 are not Johannine signals. One shepherd is truly Ezekiel’s (Ezekiel 34:23), and John uses it.
